_comment: PLAT-37 parity readings, PLAT50-FUSE pass (segmented inline-run fusion A/B).
The six per-view lane grades had never been written to any tracked file; only the MEANS were.
They are recovered here from the pass's own ink.{before,armA,after}.<view>.json, with CROP_PX and a content digest for every graded buffer.
Every figure names the commit it was measured against, per the workspace standard.
standing: RECOVERED RECORD, not a fresh capture. Every number is read back from the PLAT50-FUSE pass's persisted inkflip JSON. No frame was re-captured and no comparison was invented here.
whyRecoveredNow: The host reached 100% disk: 7.4 G free against 7.4 G of campaign capture directories. Raw .rgba/.png were stripped from every SUPERSEDED pass; PLAT50-FUSE (final arm) and FLOOR (instruments) were kept intact. The grades were extracted BEFORE anything was deleted, so the cleanup could not destroy the only copy -- which is precisely the failure the issue predicted.

subject.workspaceThisPass: codetracer/build/plat37-parity-PLAT50-FUSE/ (gitignored; RETAINED, so a re-grade from pixels is still possible)

geometry.cropProvenance: DERIVED, not read from a log -- measure-after.sh takes CROP_PX as a required parameter and persists it nowhere (provenance gap 1 of the issue). Recovered as (GPUI capture height - Electron capture height): laptop 1856-1800 = 56, wide 2216-2160 = 56. The two window sizes agreeing is the control.
geometry.whyNotThe58OfEarlierPasses: 58 was what the lane needed while the GPUI window content area was one point too tall (PLAT37-ISSUE-U). 56 is both what it reads now and the sharp FLIP minimum the 2026-10-25 alignment sweep independently found.

instrument.what: inkflip, a thin CLI over codetracer-image-diff's flip(). The SAME binary on all three arms, so the arms are on one scale.
instrument.quantity: frameFracOver0_10 -- the fraction of the frame FLIP judges perceptibly different at all. Identical to the WHOLE region's fracOver0_10 in every file checked.
instrument.scaleAgreementWithTheLane: report.py's docstring hedges that this scale 'is not the campaign's lane-grade'. Measured, the two coincide to 8 decimals on twelve independent values. The hedge is wrong; it is the third provenance gap named in the issue and should be corrected at the source.
instrument.p50AndMaxErrorRemark: p50 is 0.0 in every arm, as in every pass. maxError is constant within an alignment. Neither is a progress signal and neither is cited as one.

armMeaning.before: Fusion opt-in absent. The baseline this A/B calibrates against.
armMeaning.armA: Opt-in present but set to "0" -- provably inert. The control.

headline.readAsProgressNotVerdict: 0.3725 -> 0.10369 is the campaign arc on this proxy. fracOver0_10 is not a pass/fail gate and this lane does not gate.

worstResidualRegionsInFinalArm.note: Top 10 by shareOfError within their own view. This is where the remaining difference lives, and it is the honest answer to 'what is left'.

bufferDigests.why: PLAT37-ISSUE-W's remedy: a content digest beside every figure, so a later disagreement can be classified as a different measurement or a different capture.
bufferDigests.algorithm: md5 of the decoded RGBA8 buffer actually handed to FLIP

whatThisFileDoesNotEstablish: That the grades were independently re-derived. They are read back from the pass's own persisted JSON. The final arm's .rgba buffers are retained so a re-grade IS possible, but it was not run here.

That visual parity is achieved. fracOver0_10 is a whole-frame proxy for perceptible difference. No screenshot in this campaign has been VISUALLY reviewed against its Electron counterpart by any agent -- a separate, still-open gap, and the reason two widget-level differences (an extra leading toolbar icon; status-bar divergence) went unnoticed by the metric for the whole campaign.
Anything about the Linux lane. Every figure here is aarch64-darwin.
